title: Post-acute trauma rehabilitation
summary: Seriously and severely injured patients are often not fit for rehabilitation at the end of acute inpatient treatment as they lack the necessary ability to help themselves and still require medical/nursing treatment. For these patients, there is currently no adequate form of care in Germany to provide them with medical support until follow-up treatment/rehabilitation (AHB/ AR) without breaking the care pathway. This has clearly negative consequences for patients, as the necessary therapies to restore functionality and quality of life are severely delayed or inaccessible. The PaTronus study is investigating the extent to which a structured transfer of patients directly to post-acute trauma rehabilitation in specialized rehabilitation facilities after their acute stay is suitable for accelerating their recovery and integrating them into the regular rehabilitative care concepts AHB/AR at an earlier stage.

interventions.name: Transfer of severely and most severely injured patients who have not reached rehabilitation capability during acute hospitalization to suitable post-acute trauma rehabilitation immediately after completion of acute medical treatment and implementation of this post-acute trauma rehabilitation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- ISS > 15
- Trauma-surgical treatment initially largely completed
- Severe impairment of activity and participation to be expected
- Positive prognosis for achieving the ability to rehabilitate on discharge from post-acute rehabilitation
- Patient partially mobilized (2-4 hours wheelchair)
- Functional capacity for several therapy services daily for approx. 30 min each
- Fractures stable after exercise
- Mostly conscious, simple requests can be followed
- Able to communicate, interact, if necessary with aids
- Statutory health insurance with participating health insurance companies
Exclusion criteria:
- Rehabilitation capability given at the end of acute stay or achievable through transitional care in hospital
- No benefit commitment from payer
- Relevant CNS injuries
- Need for intensive medical monitoring/therapy
- SHT, paraplegic lesions, vegetative state with indication for neuro-rehabilitation
- Delirium
- Patients with indication for neurological post-acute or geriatric rehab
- Burn patients who take advantage of specialized treatment offers
- Suicide risk, risk of self/other endangerment
- Manifest addiction or drug addiction
- Lack of resilience due to comorbidities
- Cost units BG, private cost units or cost units not participating in the project
- Not able to communicate, not able to interact
- Ground transportation by ambulance not possible
- Participation in study refused
